title: Notification Service OOMKilled Worker Pod CrashLoop
symptoms: Worker pods entering CrashLoopBackOff state repeatedly
Notification queue backlog accumulated 45,000 pending messages
investigation_steps: Retrieved pod termination events via kubectl describe pod
Analyzed JVM heap dump and native memory profiler traces
Identified unbounded byte buffer accumulation in PDF invoice attachment generator
Found unclosed file descriptors in temporary file generation routine
findings: Invoice generator was retaining unmanaged byte buffers in global scope
Each PDF attachment leaked approximately 8MB of RAM until pod exceeded 512Mi limit
root_cause: Memory leak caused by unmanaged byte buffer retention in PDF invoice rendering library during high-volume batch dispatch.
actions_taken: Patched PDF generation logic to use streaming buffers with explicit cleanup
Temporarily bumped pod memory limit from 512Mi to 1Gi
resolution: Updated PDF rendering buffer context disposal, enforced garbage collection, and increased pod limit to 1Gi.
verification: Pod memory consumption stabilized at 190Mi under 10,000 notifications/min load with zero pod restarts.
recommendations: Implement container memory leak synthetic soak tests in staging pipeline
Add Prometheus alert for pod memory utilization > 80% with positive rate of change
engineer_feedback: Memory leak hotfix verified stable across all 6 notification worker replicas.
